brief.analysis: The engine wants to short gold's run against the S&P back toward a five-year average struck before central banks became persistent, price-insensitive buyers — that steady official demand has lifted where gold 'should' trade, so the old average is a stale target. Two facts confirm it: the stretch has already almost fully unwound (it sits just 0.73 of a normal move above average, versus a peak of 5.12), and measured against gold's own rising trend it is actually slightly cheap, not rich (detrended reading -0.67). The realistic 200-day target was already achieved; the remaining +11% to the flat mean is chasing a mean that has moved.
brief.report_line: We are short gold versus the S&P into a demand shift that has raised gold's fair level; the easy reversion is already done and the leftover 11% target chases a five-year average that structural central-bank buying has invalidated — avoid.

brief.analysis: This is the clearest broken band: the raw signal calls defense rich (1.71) but against its own trend it is barely stretched (0.66), and that gap is direct evidence the fair level is drifting upward as Europe and NATO structurally rearm. The realistic 200-day target is essentially already met (+0.7%), the forward hit rate is weak (3 of 7), the uptrend is still intact and moving averages give zero confirmation (0/3). The +18% pull to the five-year mean is betting against a spending shift, not a temporary dislocation.
brief.report_line: We are short defense versus the S&P, but its fair level is rising with structural rearmament — the near target is already met, momentum is unbroken, and the 18% mean target is a trap; avoid.

brief.analysis: Silver's explosive run ahead of gold peaked at an extreme 6.36 but has already snapped most of the way back (now 1.3), the 200-day target is achieved, and against its own trend silver is only mildly rich (0.81) — the clean part of this trade is largely behind us. Silver rides both gold's central-bank-driven strength and rising industrial/solar demand, so its fair level relative to gold has drifted up and the further 18% to the flat five-year mean is regime-exposed. Strong moving-average confirmation (3/3) keeps it tradeable, but only for the residual move, sized modestly.
brief.report_line: We are short silver versus gold after an extreme spike that has mostly reverted; confirmation is strong but the remaining 18% to the old average leans on a mean that industrial and precious demand have lifted — tradeable in small size, caution.

brief.analysis: Semiconductors have genuinely run ahead of the broad Nasdaq and remain stretched both on a flat basis (2.71) and against their own trend (2.36), so a real pullback is tradeable. But the five-year-average target implies chips fall roughly 68% relative to QQQ, which is nonsense in an AI build-out that has permanently raised the chip sector's weight — only the nearer 200-day target (about 14%) is credible. Confirmation is thin (moving-average score 1/3), so this is a size-down trade toward the near target, not the mean.
brief.report_line: We are short semiconductors versus the Nasdaq for a real near-term cooling of roughly 14%, but the AI capital-spending cycle has permanently raised chips' share so we cap the target at the 200-day line and size down — caution.

brief.analysis: Metals-and-mining's run ahead of the market has already largely reverted (now 1.32 from a 4.57 peak), the 200-day target is achieved, and against its own trend the sector is not rich (0.63) — the reliable move is done. Miners are being lifted by strong gold and silver plus copper demand from electrification and data-center power, so the fair level has drifted up and the further 21% to the flat mean is regime-exposed; the base is also thin (only 2 clean episodes). Any residual short is small and opportunistic, not a conviction reversion.
brief.report_line: We are short metals and mining versus the S&P after most of the stretch has already unwound; with the near target met and copper and precious-metal demand lifting the fair level, we treat the remaining 21% as regime-exposed and trade only small — caution.
